summary: Samiran Chandra Chakrabarti is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He held a post at the University of Calcutta from around 1970 to 2005 and served as Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society, attested in 2026.

Sampan Chakrabarty works in Indology. He completed doctoral studies under the supervision of Pallab Sengupta and held a post as a Research Scholar/Fellow at The Asiatic Society, both attested in 2026.

Samten Gyaltsen Karmay is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of London under David Snellgrove. He held posts at SOAS, CNRS, Collège de France, and was president of the IATS (1995–2000).

Samuel Beal (1825–1889) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Cambridge and Durham, he served as headmaster at Bramham College (1848–1850) and as Professor of Chinese at University College London and the University of London (1877–1889).
Samuel Johnson (1709–1784) was a scholar in linguistics. He was educated at King Edward VI School, King Edward VI College, Stourbridge (around 1726), and Pembroke College, Oxford (1728–1731).

Samuel M. Grupper is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, where he studied under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.

Samuel Wells Williams (1812–1884) was a Sinologist and linguist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute from around 1831 to 1832. He later held a post at Yale University from around 1877 to 1884.

Sandra A. Wawrytko is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She held positions at San Diego State University, attested as Professor in 1999 and as Associate Professor of Philosophy in 2014.
Sandra Bell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her doctorate at Durham University in 1991 and also held an academic post there.

Sandra Hochwarter is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed her Mag.phil. at the University of Vienna, where she studied under Anne MacDonald and wrote her MA under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.
Sang-Kyun Sun is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Delhi under the supervision of Sanghasen Singh. In 1995, he was attested as a lecturer at JinGak Buddhist College.

Sangay Dorji is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Tengtho Goenpa and Semtokha Rigney School. He later worked as a teacher at Semtokha Rigney School and served as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission.

Sangharakshita (1925–2018) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Banaras Hindu University and under teachers including Jagdish Kashyap and Jianmin Chen. He founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967.

Sangseraima Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her doctorate at the University of Oxford (around 2013–2018) and held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of California, Santa Barbara (around 2018–2020).

Sangye Khadro is a practitioner and scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Yeshe Thubten, Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.

Historian Sanjay Subrahmanyam studied at the University of Delhi. He held professorial chairs at Oxford (1993–1995, 2002), the EHESS (1995–2002), the Collège de France (2013–2021), and has been a Distinguished Professor at UCLA since 2005.
Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under the guidance of M. K. Ganguli and received traditional training from A. P. Lama.

Sanjukta Gupta is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned doctorates from Visva-Bharati University and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. She held teaching posts at Jadavpur University, Utrecht University (1968–1986), and the University of Oxford (1986–2000).

Sanki Ichikawa (1886–1970) was a Japanese linguist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (1906–1909). He served on the faculty at Tokyo Imperial University from 1916 to 1946 and at the Institute for Research in Language Teaching (~1923–1957).
Sanne Dokter-Mersch is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Leiden University between 2016 and 2021, where she was supervised by Peter C. Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi.
